title: Powerful and fast, but some trade-offs
body:
I’ve been using the HP OmniBook Ultra mainly for office work and coursework, and in terms of performance it’s been great. The AMD Ryzen AI 9 and 32GB RAM make everything feel very fast and efficient, and the 2TB SSD is plenty of space. The keyboard is comfortable to type on, the speakers are good, and the overall build feels solid and premium.

On the downside, the display feels like a downgrade coming from an ASUS OLED laptop—it’s okay, but doesn’t have the same deep blacks or vibrant colors. The hinge also isn’t very sturdy and the screen tends to wobble when I’m typing quickly. Battery life is decent and lasts me about a workday of office and coursework use, but at this price point there are laptops that do noticeably better.

One more thing to note: it only has two USB-C ports and one USB-A port. That setup can be a bit of a hassle if you’re using multiple peripherals (mouse, external drive, monitor, etc.), and you’ll pretty much need a hub or docking station to make it convenient.

Overall, it’s a very powerful and capable machine for productivity, but the screen, hinge, limited ports, and just-average battery life keep it from being perfect.

title: Disappointed and Surprised
body:
I'm a big techy/nerdy guy and I barely provide reviews online, but this one really deserves a detailed one!

I absolutely love AMD processors and specially their newer generation with dedicated NPU (so I run LLMs locally) and better discrete GPUs. Hence, this laptop was a perfect choice and beast of a configuration for Windows. Although, I don't know what's wrong with BestBuy! The first machine I got had weird BIOS issues and screen freeze and more. They replaced it with another one which has speaker issues ( a static distorted noise even on mute ).

I also have several HP cases opened to mitigate the issue. HP officially doesn't make this configuration and BestBuy (being HP's official partner) customizes these model. I am not sure what they [BestBuy] did here, but surely it messed up this machine. Maybe few folks got perfectly working one and remaining people like me ( as I see other reviews ), kept on getting this damaged machine.

To make things worse on BestBuy's end, they kept selling me their unnecessary GeekSquad membership plans to mitigate this issue as a better option over constant replacement. Also, I went to 3-4 different BestBuys, and all of them have their own rule of replacement/exchange!

This was my first ever BestBuy purchase and it's been a disappointing experience so far! At one point, I only cared about getting a good working machine but sadly with this obnoxious process, I had no hopes! Hence, I just returned the laptop eventually ( and now, I don't have anything lol).

In conclusion, once again, this is a beast of a configuration for a Windows laptop but on paper! At the end, if things don't work that well when you pay more than a grand, you really start questioning....

title: Impressive little box
body:
The HP OmniBook Ultra has been an absolute joy to use. I picked up the 14" 2.2K Touch-Screen model with the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 375, 32GB of memory, and a huge 2TB SSD, and it quickly became my daily driver for both work and play. The Meteor Silver finish looks sleek and modern, and the laptop itself feels light but extremely sturdy in hand—it’s definitely portable enough to carry around all day without a second thought.

Performance is fantastic. Whether I’m hammering away at code, running virtual machines, or crunching through photo edits, the Ryzen AI 9 chip and 32GB of RAM handle everything I throw at it without breaking a sweat. File transfers and application launches are almost instant thanks to the fast SSD, and surprisingly, even gaming works well on this system. The Radeon graphics aren’t on the level of a dedicated gaming laptop, but for casual titles and some older AAA games, it’s very capable.

Battery life also stands out—I’m regularly getting around 12–13 hours with mixed use, and it’s easy to go a full day without reaching for the charger. The laptop wakes instantly from sleep, which is great when jumping between meetings or travel. The screen is sharp, bright, and a pleasure to use for coding, writing, and media.

The keyboard and touchpad are comfortable, making long sessions easy. I love having the extra ports (Thunderbolt 4, USB-C), and the Wi-Fi 7 is noticeably fast. The only minor annoyances so far are the glossy screen, which can reflect in really bright environments, and some pre-installed HP software that I disabled pretty quickly.

Overall, the OmniBook Ultra is a fantastic all-rounder. It’s powerful, portable, lasts all day, and looks great—perfect for anyone who needs serious performance in a thin and light laptop. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it!

title: Best Buy open box fraud
body: This review is for Best Buy, not the computer itself.  I ordered from Best Buy online an Open Box--Excellent version of this computer, looking forward to its great features. Everything looked brand new when I opened the box, but in trying to set it up, it didn't display any options to connect to internet. Called HP support and after 2 hours of troubleshooting they concluded that the network adapter was not detectable. They recommended I return it to Best Buy. I did, but since open box, all they would do it give me a refund, not replace it (and no more open boxes of this model either at that price).  So I had to pay $400 more for a new one to be picked up at a store an hour away (or wait another week for them to ship me one).  They offered no discount or compensation for my trouble and hours wasted.  Since Open Box-Excellent units are supposed to be checked out, and this obviously was not, they defrauded me.  So be wary of open box deals at Best Buy!

title: Excellent build quality, snappy speed!
body:
This is one powerhouse of a laptop. With 32GB RAM, 2TB SSD storage, and the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 375 processor, you can easily handle almost any task you could think of with daily use. Very snappy, fast chip that handles daily tasks with ease. Feels like it will age well going forward. 

The built-in AI features are actually very helpful and convenient. These features will also be continually built upon and improved to become more useful in the future. Coming from using solely Apple products for most of my life, it is refreshing to see other companies out there can also get the job done. 

The build quality is excellent. The laptop feels very sturdy but is not overly heavy. It looks beautiful and has a very svelte vibe to it.

The battery life is great--I can get multiday use out of it through the week. No complaints here. 

One of my favorite features is the feel of the keyboard...it is excellent! Such a joy to type on.

Honestly for not being an OLED display and "only" being 2.2K resolution, the picture is quite good. More than enough for me and my use-case of casual web browsing, using Microsoft Office, email, etc. 

Overall, I am very impressed and happy with my purchase of this laptop. I would highly recommend to anyone thinking of buying this computer.

title: So far so good
body:
I purchased the 2TB SSD model about 10 days ago and wanted to report that installation of the operating system and initial loading of data and software went smoothly. The hardware is working well, the display is plenty good despite not being OLED, and the computer seems very responsive and quick.  I am very pleased thus far. 
Still waiting for the Microsoft Copilot + features, but
I used R Drive Image to create a pristine system image in case the Microsoft AI  updates go sideways on us. 
And I did buy an Anker 8-in-1 USB-C hub to give me extra ports for my scanners and printer.
I am not a gamer so I can't report on its gaming performance. But for everything else, I think this is a winner.
